analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Commodities 2027 Index Rebalancing Estimates
key_insights: Goldman Sachs Commodity Sales' initial estimates for the Jan-2027 GSCI and BCOM index rebalance show Precious metals flipping to net buying after several years of rebalance selling, as prices have fallen: 4.5bn of Gold buying and 3bn of Silver buying.
Silver's total rebalance buying equals 21% of an Average Day's Volume across all tenors, based on the last 2 weeks' volume.

Crude faces 85k lots of selling (about 7.9bn notional) over the rebalance period, just shy of about 2% of total open interest. This is just over half the proportion GS expects to see in products selling.
US natural gas has 2.6bn of buying at current levels, equal to 6% of aggregate open interest across all contracts.
In industrial metals, Nickel buying equals 23% of 3m ADV and Lead buying 18% of 3m ADV. Aluminum buying equals 14% of ADV on 3s.
In agriculturals, coffee has 13k contracts of buying (35% of an average day's volume). Lean Hog has 30k lots of buying (38% of an average day's volume, 9% of open interest).
The final contract amounts are a moving target. Price changes before the January roll can change them significantly.
Part of the rebalancing will occur beyond the first few contracts because of 'enhanced' exposure in the market.
The bulk of the rebalance happens on the 5th-9th business day of January, but a significant portion can be spread throughout the month.
risk_factors: Estimated rebalance flows can change significantly with price moves before the January roll.
Part of the rebalance occurs beyond the first few contracts and can be spread through January, so timing of flows is uncertain.
vol_and_positioning: Index rebalance flows for Jan-2027: Gold buying 4.5bn, Silver buying 3bn (21% of ADV), Crude selling about 7.9bn notional (85k lots, about 2% of OI), US NG buying 2.6bn (6% of OI), Lean Hog buying 30k lots (38% of ADV, 9% of OI), Coffee buying 13k contracts (35% of ADV).
